title: Porch Light
author: Fixture Poet
text:
The porch light stays on past the hour anyone is expected.
Moths find it before people do.

I sit under it anyway, reading nothing,
watching the street settle into itself for the night.

Somewhere a screen door closes twice, then a third time,
as if someone can't decide whether to stay in or out.

The light draws a small yellow circle on the steps,
just wide enough for one chair and one cup going cold.

I could go inside. Nothing is keeping me here
except the particular privacy of being visible and alone,
lit up for anyone passing to see and not stop for,
which is, some nights, exactly what I want.
